subject: Duel resolution order
claim: The repository does not yet establish the ordering of combat phases, player move submission, server resolution, participant updates, and client-visible effects in a duel; this finding records the evidence gap rather than asserting a combat protocol.
how_to_repeat: Use two disposable accounts and an Ambrose server bound only to loopback, with a deterministic test duel against an authored opponent.
Capture the private loopback session from duel entry through one completed round, including the planning timer, both move submissions, resolution, health/effect updates, and the next-round boundary.

Record only message names, service and order identifiers, directions, frame ordering, payload lengths, participant counts, and client-visible state transitions; keep captures, addresses, credentials, and payload bytes private.
Repeat with one player passing and the other selecting a single-target spell, then with the submission order reversed.
Compare the metadata-only traces to determine whether the server resolves by team, slot, submission time, or another ordering, and which message marks the round boundary.
evidence: The contributor-track lists F-01 as an open combat finding for duel resolution order and the messages exchanged at each step.

The phase 9 roadmap names combat messages such as MSG_COMBATPHASE, MSG_COMBATMOVE, MSG_COMBATACTIONS, MSG_COMBATHEALTH, MSG_COMBATUPFIRST, and MSG_COMBATMOVESELECTION, but does not provide a verified end-to-end trace.
The phase 11 roadmap requires team and slot-order execution while separately identifying real-client acceptance checks; no repository finding currently proves that ordering.
disproof: A private, repeatable duel trace or simulator-backed finding establishes the complete message ordering and resolution rule; that evidence should replace this gap record rather than be treated as confirmation of it.
